Keywords: Salihids Zokomos the Mighty Sovereign Authority
RagShortTexts: In 374 AD, Salihids governed from Jordanian Desert & Petra Environs, under the paramount rule of Salihid Phylarchs.
The polity asserted sovereign legitimacy anchored in Salihids dynastic heritage and royal assemblies.
Surrounded by shifting imperial and tribal pressures, the regime enforced loyalty through binding oaths and martial law.

Variants.Content: In 374 AD, the sovereign authority of Salihids anchored itself within Jordanian Desert & Petra Environs, confronting the accelerating tremors of Late Antiquity. Governed by Salihid Phylarchs, the state projected imperial legitimacy through dynastic lineage, military patronage, and strict codification of feudal oaths. Emphasizing institutional doctrine rooted in Salihids heritage, the crown mobilized loyal retinues and aristocratic councils to repel external encroachment. Beneath ceremonial grandeur lay unceasing vigilance against shifting steppe incursions and frontier uprisings, compelling the leadership to bind provincial magnates to the throne through land redistribution and martial alliance, safeguarding royal continuity amid an era of continent-wide transition.

Riders of the phylarch's guard oil their lances by the fire before the standard is raised. When the Salihid Phylarchs' banner moves, every man mounts and rides out with a shield on his arm. Blood spent in battle is repaid with water rights and grants of pasture, and the riders know a grant is only as good as the phylarch's word. At the Salihids post, the night watchword is "Wolf."

The tribal sheikhs measure the phylarch's orders against their wells before they comply. Oaths are sworn in the council tent, yet the clans keep their wells, their tolls, and their privileges. Each sealed letter between them repeats one condition: the phylarch's authority holds only while tribal rights are respected.
